To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neocortex generates complex seizures with SW/ PSW complexes and fast runs and that RE and TC cells are involved in these seizures as a function of their membrane potential.
the neocortex, and not the thalamus or any other brain structure, is the generator of the seizures with spike-wave complexes and fast runs that are the hallmark of the Lennox-Gas-taut syndrome.
the thalamus, as a relay station between cortex and brainstem, does not play a major role in the generation of SW/PSW seizures, but rather reflects cortical activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and network mechanisms of neocortically generated seizures.
the mechanisms of seizure initiation, synchronization, and termination, and the role of thalamic nuclei in these processes.
the generation and propagation of seizures in the neocortex.

neocortex generates the seizures and that the dorsal thalamus is not a necessary structure in the generation and maintenance of these seizures.
neocortex, not the thalamus, is the primary site of generation of seizures with SW/ PSW complexes and fast runs.
neocortex, and not thalamus, is the source of seizures with SW/ PSW complexes and fast runs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cortical neurons are responsible for seizure generation and thalamic cells for seizure modulation.
cortical seizures are generated in the neocortex and thalamus is involved in the expression of the seizures as a result of its anatomical and physiological relationship with the neocortex.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the neocortex is a self-sustained generator of complex seizures and that the thalamus plays a secondary and modulatory role.
cortical networks generate seizures with SW/ PSW complexes and fast runs that may be considered as two distinct seizure components, each having its own origin and cellular mechanisms.
the neocortex, and not the thalamus, should be the focus of therapeutic interventions for seizures with SW/ PSW complexes.
